messages.onboarding.intro: Sign in once with your {{.Council.Name}} {{.Council.Terms.portal}} details. p.stonn keeps an encrypted session so it can update your permit for you.
messages.onboarding.email_pinned: Your {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account must use this same email — it can’t be changed here.
messages.onboarding.reset_beside: Forgot it — or never set one? {{slot "reset"}}Reset it at the council{{endslot}}, then link here.
messages.onboarding.saved_password_why: It is stored encrypted and used only to sign back in when the council ends the session, which happens whenever you sign in to the {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}} yourself.
messages.onboarding.rejected_lead: Either the password is wrong, or your {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account isn’t under {{slot "b"}}{{.User.Email}}{{endslot}}.
messages.onboarding.rejected_reset: • {{slot "b"}}Forgot your council password — or never set one?{{endslot}} {{slot "reset"}}Reset it at the council{{endslot}}, then come back and link. This is the most common fix.
messages.onboarding.rejected_try_portal: Unsure which it is? Try your details at the council’s own {{slot "portal"}}{{.Council.Terms.portal_site}}{{endslot}} first.
messages.onboarding.throttled_password: • Your password — try it at the council’s own {{slot "portal"}}{{.Council.Terms.portal_site}}{{endslot}}. If it fails there too, {{slot "reset"}}reset it at the council{{endslot}}.
messages.onboarding.picker_error: If this keeps happening, check the council's own {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}} is working.
messages.onboarding.picker_none: If you expected a visitor permit here, check it on the council's own {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}}: it may have expired, or be held by another resident at your address. It's also possible the council changed something on its side that p.stonn doesn't recognise yet
messages.onboarding.picker_apply: Apply for a visitor permit on the council's {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}} first, then come back and it will appear here.
messages.settings.password_saved: Your password is saved (encrypted) so p.stonn can sign back in on its own if the council ends your session. Note: signing in to the {{.Council.Short}} {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}} yourself still logs p.stonn out until the next reconnect.
messages.settings.password_not_saved: Your password isn't saved. If the council ends your session — including when you sign in to the {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}} yourself — you'll need to re-link by hand. To turn this on, unlink and link again with “Save my password” ticked.
messages.terms.next_step: Next you’ll connect your council account, which takes your {{slot "b"}}{{.Council.Terms.portal}} password{{endslot}}. Not sure you have one? {{slot "reset"}}Reset it at the council{{endslot}} while you’re here.
messages.guest.credit: This permit is managed with {{slot "home"}}p.stonn{{endslot}} — free for {{.Council.Name}} residents.
messages.guest.own_household: Does your own household juggle a visitor permit? p.stonn is free for {{.Council.Name}} residents.
messages.guests.poster_foot: Set up with p.stonn · an unofficial {{.Council.Name}} permit helper
messages.share.intro: Free for any {{.Council.Short}} household with a visitor parking permit. If someone you know is still changing the plate by hand, here’s how to send it their way.
messages.share.poster_lead: Your {{.Council.Short}} visitor parking permit, on a schedule.
messages.share.poster_note: A weekly roster for regulars, one-off bookings for everyone else, and a link or QR code your visitors can use themselves. Free for {{.Council.Name}} residents.
messages.public.hero_note: A free service for {{.Council.Name}} residents ({{.Council.SuburbList}}). Sign in with a one-time code sent to your email.
messages.public.need_account: You'll need an existing {{.Council.Name}} {{slot "b"}}{{.Council.Terms.portal}}{{endslot}} account with a visitor permit on it. Sign in here with {{slot "b"}}the same email address your {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account uses{{endslot}} — p.stonn can only connect to the council account that matches. It schedules a permit you already hold; it can't apply for one. {{slot "how"}}What you need →{{endslot}}
messages.public.step_link: Sign in with your {{.Council.Terms.portal}} email, then connect with your council password.
messages.public.disclaimer: An unofficial app, not affiliated with or endorsed by the {{.Council.Name}}. You remain responsible for your permit and any fines. {{slot "security"}}Security & data{{endslot}}
messages.public.about_unofficial: p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool for scheduling your {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permit. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the council. For what it does, see {{slot "how"}}How it works{{endslot}}.
messages.public.faq_unofficial: p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool for scheduling your {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permit. It is not affiliated with the council. For what it does, see {{slot "how"}}How it works{{endslot}}.
messages.public.history: {{.Council.Short}} Council changed how resident and visitor parking permits work in 2026. Paper visitor permits have been phased out in favour of a digital system. The digital permit requires you to enter vehicle registration numbers into the council's online system, which is checked by parking officers as they patrol the streets.
messages.public.attempt: p.stonn is an attempt to make that easier. Once you have a permit set up with {{.Council.Terms.parking_brand}}, you can use it to set which car is on the permit each day of the week, add one-off bookings, and hand a visitor a QR link that puts their car on when they arrive.
messages.public.before_intro: p.stonn does not replace the council's system. It works on top of a permit you already hold, so you need a {{.Council.Name}} {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account with at least one visitor permit first.
messages.public.council_pages: The council’s own pages: {{slot "apply"}}visitor parking permits{{endslot}} and {{slot "faq"}}parking permit FAQs{{endslot}}.
messages.public.faq_more: p.stonn is a free, unofficial tool and is not affiliated with the {{.Council.Name}}. {{T "public.council_pages" .}} See also {{slot "how"}}how p.stonn works{{endslot}} and the {{slot "faq_page"}}FAQ{{endslot}}.
messages.capacity.full: p.stonn is full at the moment. It's run by one person for a small number of {{.Council.Short}} households, and taking on more right now would make it slower and less reliable for everyone already using it. Please try again in a while, or get in touch and I'll let you know when there's room.
messages.picker.session_rejected: Your council password was accepted — the sign-in itself worked. But when p.stonn then asked the council for your permit list, the council turned the request away. That usually means the {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account isn't fully set up yet — for example it was only just created, or doesn't have a permit on it. Entering your password here again won't change this. Please sign in at the council's own site ({{.Council.PortalHost}}) and check your visitor permit appears there, then come back and link again. If the permit is there and this keeps happening, please get in touch via the contact form.
messages.schedule.added_expired: That permit was added, but it is no longer active at the council, so nothing will be applied to it. It's under “Permits no longer active” below — renew it on the council's {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}}, then copy its schedule onto the new permit when it appears here.
messages.mail.provenance: You received this at {{.To}} because {{.Reason}}. p.stonn is a free, unofficial scheduler for {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permits.
messages.mail.referral_line: Know another {{.Council.Short}} household with a visitor permit? Send them p.stonn.org.
messages.mail.invite_lead: {{.Owner}} has given you shared access to their p.stonn account, which schedules a {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permit.
messages.mail.nudge_connect: Connecting takes one sign-in with your {{.Council.Name}} {{.Council.Terms.portal}} details. Three things trip most people up:
messages.mail.nudge_password: 1. The {{.Council.Terms.portal}} password. Forgot it — or never set one?
messages.mail.nudge_email: 2. An {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account under a different email address. p.stonn can only connect to the {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account registered under the address you signed up with ({{.To}}). If your council account uses a different address, sign in to p.stonn with that one instead.
messages.mail.nudge_apply: No {{.Council.Terms.portal}} account or visitor permit yet? Apply for a visitor permit on the council's {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}} first, then come back.
messages.mail.guest_lead: {{.Owner}} has given you a link to put a car on their {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permit ({{.Label}}).
messages.mail.guest_promo: Got a visitor permit of your own? p.stonn is free for {{.Council.Name}} residents — p.stonn.org
messages.mail.fortnight_line: If it's been handy, you might know someone else in {{.Council.Short}} with a visitor permit who'd get some use out of it too.
messages.mail.referral_lead: {{.Sender}} uses p.stonn to look after their {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permit, and thought it might be useful for you too.
messages.mail.referral_body: p.stonn changes the car on your visitor permit for you — a weekly roster for regulars, one-off bookings for everyone else, and a link or QR code your visitors can use themselves. It's free for {{.Council.Short}} residents.
messages.mail.renewal_body:
Hi,

Your visitor-permit scheduler is still running and updating your permit automatically.

We haven't seen you in p.stonn for a while, so this is a check that you still want it running. If you do nothing, it will stop on {{.When}} and you'll need to link your council account again.

(Opening p.stonn and signing in does the same thing as clicking below — either way the clock resets.)

Confirm and keep it running (one click):
{{.URL}}

If you no longer want the service, just ignore this email and it will stop on its own.

-- p.stonn
messages.seo.landing_title: {{.Council.Short}} visitor parking permits, on a schedule — p.stonn
messages.seo.landing_desc: Free tool to schedule the car on your {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permit — a weekly roster, a family link, or a QR code for tradies. Unofficial.
messages.seo.how_title: How p.stonn manages your {{.Council.Short}} visitor permit
messages.seo.how_desc: Connect your {{.Council.Short}} {{.Council.Terms.portal}} login once; p.stonn sets your visitor permit to your weekly car schedule, plus one-off changes and guest QR links.

messages.seo.contact_desc: Questions about p.stonn, the free scheduler for {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permits? Get in touch.

messages.faq.safe_q: Is it safe to give p.stonn my {{.Council.Terms.portal}} login?
messages.faq.which_council_a: The {{.Council.Name}}'s visitor parking permits (the {{.Council.Terms.portal}} system) — covering {{.Council.SuburbList}}. It does not support other councils yet.
messages.guide.signin_step: Sign in at {{slot "portal"}}{{.Council.PortalHost}}{{endslot}} — {{slot "register"}}register{{endslot}} first if you haven’t, or {{slot "reset"}}reset your password{{endslot}} if you’ve never used it.
messages.guide.change_title: How do I change the car on my {{.Council.Short}} visitor permit? — p.stonn
messages.guide.change_desc: Changing the vehicle on a {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permit: the steps on the council's {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}}, and how to stop doing it by hand.
messages.guide.change_h1: How do I change the car on my {{.Council.Short}} visitor permit?
messages.guide.change_para: On the council's {{.Council.Terms.portal_site}}: sign in, choose Update Vehicle on the permit, enter the new plate, save. It has to be done before each visitor parks.
messages.guide.change_note: You can also ring the council on {{.Council.Phone}} to have the vehicle changed.
messages.guide.carer_title: Visitor parking for a cleaner, nanny or carer in {{.Council.Short}} — p.stonn
messages.guide.carer_desc: A {{.Council.Name}} visitor permit covers one car at a time. How to handle a cleaner, nanny or carer who comes every week without changing the plate by hand.
messages.guide.carer_h1: Visitor parking for a cleaner, nanny or carer in {{.Council.Short}}
messages.guide.carer_note: Carer arrangements can also qualify for a physical permit under the council’s {{slot "apply"}}exceptional circumstances{{endslot}} provision — worth asking about if the online system doesn’t suit your household.
messages.guide.paper_title: Do visitors need a paper permit in {{.Council.Short}}? — p.stonn
messages.guide.paper_desc: {{.Council.Name}} visitor parking permits are digital by default: nothing to display, but the number plate has to be right before each visitor parks. What that means in practice.
messages.guide.paper_h1: Do visitors need a paper permit in {{.Council.Short}}?
messages.guide.paper_note: Physical permits: see {{slot "apply"}}the council’s visitor-permit page{{endslot}} for the exceptional-circumstances application, or ring {{.Council.Phone}}.
